question: im a freshman and kinda lost. whats the difference between a major, gen eds, and electives? do they all count toward the 128 credits

question: do I have to declare a major right away or can I stay undecided for a bit

body.answer:
You can stay undeclared for a while, but not indefinitely. Ramapo says undergraduate students pursuing a bachelor’s degree must declare in their sophomore year before completing 64 credits [7]; matriculated students must declare by 64 credits toward graduation [10]. After completing 64 credits, you are considered a junior and must have declared [2]. For an undeclared student with at least 48 but fewer than 64 credits who is enrolled for a subsequent term, the college gives notice to declare before registering for more than 64 credits; a registration hold prevents registration if you try to register for 64 or more credits without a major. Submit the online Major/Minor Declaration form to the Registrar; upon receipt, it removes the hold and you can register [10].

If you intend to graduate in four years, aim to declare during sophomore year. Most majors take at least two years to complete and usually have foundation classes you can take in your first year; some sequential science majors should be started right away. Recommended Graduation Plans can help plan your first semester [3].

Undeclared students are advised through the Ramapo Exploration Program (REP) by academic advisors in the Center for Student Success [6]. Contact the Center for Student Success for advisement: (201) 684-7441 or success@ramapo.edu [5]. As an undeclared student, select “No Changes” if you do not wish to declare now [8].

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/advisement-by-year/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/major/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/school-liaisons/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/declare-major-minor-certificate/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/declare-major-minor-certificate/) [10](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#declaring-a-major1)

question: what are the gen ed requirements at ramapo? like how many classes in each category

body.answer:
Ramapo students take 10 General Education courses: [12]
- 4 keystone courses: First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102 (within the first 64 credits), and Studies in the Arts & Humanities. [12]
- 1 course in each of 4 keystone categories: Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning (within the first 64 credits). [12]
- 1 course in 2 of 3 distribution categories: Culture & Creativity; Systems, Sustainability, & Society; and Values & Ethics. At least one distribution course must be offered by a school other than the one housing your major. [12]
The Provost page says that starting Fall 2026 the “out of school requirement” is no longer enforced in degree audit tools; it names the third category “Social Systems and Society,” unlike section 12. The pages differ on enforcement and category wording. [11][12]
Students transferring with at least 48 credits (and returning students with at least 48 Ramapo credits at re-enrollment) have some requirements waived, but still must take Critical Reading and Writing 102, Quantitative Reasoning, Scientific Reasoning, and one course from each of two distribution categories at Ramapo. Advisement identifies what remains. [9]
Approved Gen Ed courses: https://catalog.ramapo.edu/college-wide-programs/gened#general-education-categories-and-courses [10]. Curriculum map: https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/wp-content/uploads/sites/380/2023/06/General-Education-Curriculum-Map-2019-2020.pdf [12]

question: Can you tell me what the Critical Reading and Writing course is and whether everyone has to take it?

body.answer:
CRWT 101, Critical Reading and Writing I, is a 4-credit course that develops critical reading and writing skills, including analyzing texts, rhetorical strategies, MLA formatting, information literacy, and revision. It is writing intensive. [3] CRWT 101S covers the same material and includes one additional weekly class meeting for support. [4][6]

Not everyone takes CRWT 101: it is the first course in the progression, and placement determines where students begin. [6][7][9] CRWT 101 requires CRWT 080 or CRWT 090, or qualifying ACCUPLACER scores. [3] Students placed into developmental courses should plan to register for and complete them before or during their first semester. [10]

All Ramapo students must complete Critical Reading and Writing II (CRWT 102) as a General Education keystone course; CRWT 102 must be taken within the first 64 credits. [14][15] Students with an SAT Evidence-Based Reading & Writing score of 620 or higher are placed in CRWT 102. [8] Ramapo requires entering students to take the Reading/Essay Placement Test to determine appropriate course placement. [7]

question: what are the required courses for the music major and are there any that need an audition to get into

body.answer:
The Music BA has five concentrations, so requirements vary. MUSI 255 Music, History and Culture and MUSI 450 Capstone Seminar in Music are required in every concentration. [1]

• Music Production: MUSI 255; MUSI 120, 123, 210, 223, 261, 363; CNTP 388; MUSI 450. Also select 1 course from each Music and Culture list, 2 production courses and 1 elective; earn 4 group-performance credits. [1]
• Music Studies: MUSI 123, 210, 255, 316; MUSI 450. Also select 3 200-level and 3 upper-level Music and Culture courses, 1 international focus course, 1 related disciplines course, 1 co-op/internship or independent study; earn 4 performance credits. [1]

The lists of courses you may select from are at the [Music BA catalog page](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-MUSI). question: What should a freshman math major take first semester? calc 1 right away or something else

body.answer:
Mathematics is offered as a BS major [1]. The pages don’t give a current freshman’s exact first-semester schedule or say that every Mathematics major should start in Calculus I; the placement score determines the calculus-track course. If you plan to take MATH 121 Calculus I, you must take the Calculus Placement Test before registering [11]. The test assesses material from intermediate algebra through pre-calculus [4].

Use the Advanced Algebra and Functions score on your report: 280–300 places you in MATH 121, MATH 237, or MATH 205; 260–279 in MATH 110 Pre-Calculus; 200–259 in MATH 024 [8]. MATH 024 is non-credit-bearing and prepares you for Pre-Calculus; MATH 110/121/122/237 are college-level calculus-track courses [2]. A score of 3 on AP Calculus AB or BC allows you to register for MATH 121 without the placement test, but gives no credit. AP Calculus AB score 4 or 5 gives credit for Calculus I; BC score 4 or 5 gives credit for Calculus I and II, and both exempt you from the placement test [4].

For help interpreting your placement or deciding your schedule, contact the Testing Center: testing@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7441 [4].

To be granted an overload, you must have above a 3.0 GPA or be a graduating senior… (see https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/policies/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/policies/)

Unless you are undeclared, you are assigned to a faculty advisor in your major. \(page: “Unless you are undeclared, you are assigned to a faculty advisor in your major.”\) (see https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/advisement-by-year/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/advisement-by-year/)

question: Can credits from a graduate certificate be applied toward the master's degree later, and how many transfer?

body.answer:
Ramapo says academic certificates are usually made up of credit-bearing courses, but the pages don’t specifically confirm whether credits earned in a graduate certificate will count toward a later master’s degree. [4]

For Ramapo master’s programs, the policy says it may be possible to apply Ramapo master’s-level coursework to two different master’s programs, up to 15 credits or 25% of the degree’s total required credits, whichever is greater. The coursework must meet the subsequent program’s criteria, and its Program Director must permit it. [2][5] The Program Director evaluates proposed transfer credit, and the decision is final, with no appeal. [5]

Office of the Provost: provost@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7330; first floor of the Birch Mansion. [2]

Sources: [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#certificate-programs1) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#transferring-academic-credit1)

question: I have 30 credits from my previous master's at another school. Will you accept them, and how many credits would I still need for the MBA?

body.answer:
The MBA is listed as a Ramapo graduate program [1].

Your 30 credits are not automatically accepted. A course may be considered if its syllabus shows it is equivalent to a course in a Ramapo graduate program, and the course must be from another accredited higher education institution. The MBA Program Director must approve transfer credit; acceptance criteria vary by program. No more than 25% of the degree’s required credits may be considered for transfer, including GPLA credits [2, 4]. The pages don’t establish whether your particular credits will be approved.

The pages don’t state the MBA’s total required credits or how many you personally would still need. They describe a 30-credit MBA program for Advanced Standing only: a bachelor’s degree in Business is required; a Business minor and/or completed foundation Business coursework may be considered subject to MBA Program Director approval [5].

Graduate Admissions can direct you to the MBA Program Director: graduate@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7270 [4].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/faqs/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/requirements/)

question: Should I do the MBA or the MSN if I want to move into hospital management? Which one pays more?

body.answer:
I can’t recommend one over the other. Ramapo describes the MSN as a 34/35-credit program, offered online with some hybrid features, with a Nurse Administration track [2]. The provided pages don’t compare MBA and MSN pay, so I don’t have verified information about which pays more.

Graduate Admissions can help with program questions: graduate@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7270; text (201) 800-6057; fax (201) 684-7964; McBride House.

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/home/)
